newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns Americans of potential terrorist acts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns Americans of potential terrorist acts.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it had received threats of increased terrorist attacks over the next two weeks in Israel and the West Bank and warned Americans there to exercise caution.

"There are indications of an increased likelihood of terrorist attacks over the next two weeks. U.S. citizens (in Israel, Jerusalem and the West Bank) are advised to exercise caution in public areas, to avoid travel on public buses, to avoid congregating at bus stops," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
Burns said: "We're issuing a travel advisory today on Israel, Jerusalem and the West Bank. It warns American citizens about the potential for terrorist actions in those areas."

"While Americans have not been specifically targeted, Americans have been kiled in the past in those areas in terrorist incidents," so it was Washington's responsibility to make them aware of the new threats, he said.
Burns said the threats were general, meaning no specific times or venues for attacks were mentioned.

The warning came as tensions ran high as Israelis and Palestinians still negotiating redeployment of Israeli forces from the West Bank town of Hebron. An Israeli soldier sprayed rifle fire into a Hebron market Wednesday, wounding seven Arabs in what he called an attempt to keep the town from being handed over to Palestinian rule.

Burns said the U.S. warning was issued "because of some information that we have and I think it's also because the general climate is so volatile and the terrorist shooting in Hebron yesterday is an example of that."
